title: Statistics - Lesson 3: Interquartile Range Assessment
description: Checkpoint assessment for calculating and interpreting interquartile range.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the interquartile range?
options: The spread of the middle 50 percent of ordered data
The difference between the maximum and minimum
The middle value of the whole data set
The sum of all values divided by the number of values
questions.explanation: The IQR is Q3 - Q1, so it measures how spread out the middle half of the data is.

questions.question: Order the data 18, 12, 30, 24, 16, 21, 27 and enter the median only.
questions.explanation: The ordered data are 12, 16, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. The middle value is 21.

questions.question: Find the IQR of 12, 16, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30.
questions.explanation: Leave out the median 21. The lower half is 12, 16, 18, so Q1 = 16. The upper half is 24, 27, 30, so Q3 = 27. IQR = 27 - 16 = 11.

questions.question: For a data set with an odd number of values, this lesson's method leaves the median out of both halves when finding Q1 and Q3.
questions.explanation: That is the convention used in the lesson examples: the median splits the data, then each half is used to find Q1 and Q3.

questions.question: A five-number summary is minimum 4, Q1 9, median 13, Q3 22, maximum 40. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 22 - 9 = 13. The minimum and maximum are not used for IQR.

questions.question: A student says the IQR of 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 25 is 22 because 25 - 3 = 22. What did the student calculate?
questions.explanation: Maximum minus minimum is the range. IQR uses Q3 - Q1.

questions.question: Group A has Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 18. Group B has Q1 = 10 and Q3 = 25. Which group has the more consistent middle 50 percent?
options: There is not enough information to find either IQR
questions.explanation: Group A has IQR 6. Group B has IQR 15. The smaller IQR shows Group A's middle 50 percent is more consistent.

questions.question: A larger IQR always means the data set is better.
questions.explanation: A larger IQR only means the middle 50 percent is more spread out. Whether that is good depends on the situation.

questions.question: The IQR of quiz scores is 14 points. Interpret this in one sentence.
questions.correctAnswer: The middle 50 percent of quiz scores vary by 14 points.
questions.explanation: A complete interpretation names the middle 50 percent, the spread, and the context or unit: quiz scores in points.

questions.question: Why is IQR often useful when a data set has an unusually high maximum?
options: It does not directly use the maximum value.
It changes the maximum into the median.
It makes the data set have no outliers.
It is always larger than the range.
questions.explanation: IQR uses Q1 and Q3, so an extreme maximum does not directly enter the calculation.

questions.question: Find Q1 for the ordered data 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The median is 10, so the lower half is 4, 6, 8. The median of the lower half is Q1 = 6.

questions.question: Find Q3 for the ordered data 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The median is 10, so the upper half is 12, 14, 16. The median of the upper half is Q3 = 14.

questions.question: Explain the difference between range and IQR in one or two sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: Range is maximum minus minimum and measures the spread of the whole data set. IQR is Q3 minus Q1 and measures the spread of the middle 50 percent.
questions.explanation: The key distinction is which values are used: range uses the extremes, while IQR uses the first and third quartiles.

questions.question: For the data 10, 12, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, what is the IQR?
questions.explanation: The median is 18. The lower half is 10, 12, 12, 15, so Q1 = 12. The upper half is 20, 22, 25, 28, so Q3 = 23.5. IQR = 23.5 - 12 = 11.5.
